name.text: Negative Angles and Trigonometric Ratios Using the CAST Rule

questiontext.text:
Consider the negative angle: \(\theta={@theta@}\text{ radians}.\)

Remember that negative angles are measured clockwise from the positive x-axis.

(a) Identify the quadrant in which the terminal arm of the angle lies.

Enter your answer as a quadrant number (III or IV).

[[input:ans0]]

[[validation:ans0]]

(b) Determine the positive reference angle \(\alpha\), expressed in radians.

[[input:ans_ref]]

[[validation:ans_ref]]

(c) Using the reference angle and the CAST rule, calculate the exact values of the following trigonometric ratios:

\(\sin(\theta)\)

[[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]]

\(\cos(\theta)\)

[[input:ans2]]

[[validation:ans2]]

\(\tan(\theta)\)

[[input:ans3]]

[[validation:ans3]]

Instructions:

  • Give all answers in exact form.
  • Do not use decimal approximations.
  • Remember that negative angles are measured clockwise.

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

We are given:

\(\theta={@theta@}\).

Step 1: Identify the quadrant

Negative angles are measured clockwise from the positive x-axis.

The given angle is located in quadrant:

Quadrant: {@if q<=2 then "IV" else "III"@}.

Recall the CAST rule:

  • Quadrant I: All trigonometric ratios are positive.
  • Quadrant II: Sine is positive.
  • Quadrant III: Tangent is positive.
  • Quadrant IV: Cosine is positive.

Step 2: Determine the reference angle

The reference angle is the acute positive angle between the terminal arm and the x-axis.

For the given angle, the reference angle is:

\(\alpha={@alpha@}\).

Step 3: Determine the standard trigonometric values

Using the reference angle:

\(\sin(\alpha)={@sin_mag@}\) \(\cos(\alpha)={@cos_mag@}\) \(\tan(\alpha)={@tan_mag@}\)

Step 4: Apply the CAST rule

Sine: Sine is negative in both the third and fourth quadrants.

\(\sin(\theta)={@ta_sin@}\).

Cosine: Cosine is positive in quadrant IV and negative in quadrant III.

\(\cos(\theta)={@ta_cos@}\).

Tangent: Tangent is negative in quadrant IV and positive in quadrant III.

\(\tan(\theta)={@ta_tan@}\).

Final Answers

The correct trigonometric ratios are:

\(\sin(\theta)={@ta_sin@}\) \(\cos(\theta)={@ta_cos@}\) \(\tan(\theta)={@ta_tan@}\)
